prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My neighbour's grandson / is only / five month old.
explanation: A plural numeral requires the plural noun, or a hyphenated adjectival form: 'five months old' (or 'a five-month-old baby'). Correct to 'five months old'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market.
explanation: After a definite numeral, 'dozen' stays singular, so 'two dozens' must be 'two dozen mangoes'; the plural 'dozens' is used only in vague expressions like 'dozens of mangoes'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Only five minutes time (a) / was allowed for each speaker (b) / during the function. (c) / No error (d)
explanation: A time period used as a possessive modifier needs an apostrophe or a hyphenated singular form: 'Only five minutes' time' (or 'a five-minute time'), not 'five minutes time'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Balloons filled with helium travel hundreds or even thousands of miles.
explanation: No error: the plural subject 'Balloons' agrees with 'travel', and 'hundreds or even thousands of miles' is the correct vague-number form with 'of'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The judge decided that / the defendant was guilty of all charges, / and a five years punishment / in prison was appropriate.
options: the defendant was guilty of all charges,
explanation: When a numeral phrase modifies a noun it becomes a singular compound adjective, so 'a five years punishment' should be 'a five-year punishment'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I am thirty-two / year old and / my sister is fifteen.
explanation: In the predicative form 'X years old', the noun stays plural, so 'thirty-two year old' should be 'thirty-two years old' (hyphenated singular only when used before a noun, e.g. 'a thirty-two-year-old man').

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Abhiram returned to the signal / and gave his last hundred rupees note / to the man / who had said he needed help.
options: who had said he needed help
and gave his last hundred rupees note
explanation: As a compound adjective before 'note', the numeral phrase must be singular: 'his last hundred-rupee note', not 'hundred rupees note'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Ten-miles distance (a) / is too long to cover (b) / on foot. (c) / No error (d)
explanation: Used attributively before 'distance', the measure must be singular: 'Ten-mile distance' (or 'a distance of ten miles'), not 'Ten-miles distance'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The commanding officer instructed his infantry (A) / to take a two-miles walk (B) / down the rugged mountain terrain. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The commanding officer instructed his infantry
explanation: When a numeral plus noun works as a compound adjective before another noun, the noun stays singular: 'a two-mile walk'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The manager rejected his application (A) / because he had not attached (B) / two passport-size photographs. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: No Error — the past perfect 'had not attached' correctly precedes the past action 'rejected', and 'passport-size photographs' is the right compound form.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He purchased three dozens bananas (A) / from the local fruit vendor (B) / to distribute among the children. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: After a definite number, 'dozen' stays singular: 'three dozen bananas', not 'three dozens bananas'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

explanation: A numeral adjective used before a noun stays singular and hyphenated — 'an eight-year-old girl'.
